what_this_is: Every `contested` case on the map, ranked for an outside-sourcing pass. The job is to move a case from `contested` to `documented` by finding evidence outside the lender — a national judgment, a state audit report, a national newspaper — not to add cases. Nothing is removed from this file: it ranks.
rules: The screen ranks and never drops. BRIEF22's sentence-drop screen destroyed about one real case in nine when measured blind against 57 settled outcomes.
An index is named here, not asserted to work. Only Kenya Law is proven, in round 38. Test each route at the start of the round and record the failure by route, never by host.
A writer verifies the hooks on the card; it does not go hunting. If a hook turns out to be absent from the card's own documents, that is a correction to the card.
Moving a case to `documented` needs the outside source to carry the core harm, not to mention the project. The owner's standard is unchanged.
Ask for any missing `whole`, `conditions` or `ct` on the same card in the same pass.

The figures count properties and buildings, not people, so the number displaced is not known from them; the city says social compensation was paid to people who had to be relocated but publishes no count. The EIB's own dates do not sit together easily: the Complaints Mechanism report says the first tranche of USD 56 million was signed on 6 August 2018 and has been disbursed, with footnote 4 attaching that tranche to Metro Line 1, and the same report says the EIB approved financing of Metro Line One on 5 February 2025. The IDB and the IBRD are named in the future tense - the project "will be partly financed by further loans from" them - with no amounts, and the city dated their approved funds to September 2025, after the demolitions counted here; the EIB tranche of 2018 is the financing that was in place while the properties were being taken. The shop owner's losses on Calle 72 are his allegations, recorded by the office, which had not reported any findings. The Early Warning System record for EIB-20220741 lists an investment of USD 430 million and a project cost of USD 5,789 million as at disclosure on 20 December 2024, which are different again from the report's figures; no source reconciles them.

queue.place: Myitsone, confluence of the Mali and N'Mai rivers, Kachin State, Myanmar
companies: State Power Investment Corporation (formerly China Power Investment)
queue.confidence_note: Most relocations in 2009-2010 came before the early-2011 CDB loan and are not treated as lender-linked; the March 2012 army eviction and later exclusion from farms came after the loan but after the project was suspended, and the loan's status after suspension is unknown (AidData). CPI reported compensation of 4.1 billion kyat and US$25 million for resettlement (Wikipedia).

queue.title: Panguna Copper Mine and the Jaba River
queue.place: Panguna, Bougainville, Papua New Guinea
lenders: Conzinc Rio Tinto of Australia / Rio Tinto, through Bougainville Copper Ltd (foreign investor)
queue.confidence_note: Health and species claims rest on Wikipedia's summary. Rio Tinto says it complied with the law during mining and has refused to fund remediation (Wikipedia). The legacy impact assessment by Tetra Tech Coffey reported in 2024 that tailings and chemicals continue to be released, causing environmental, social, health and human rights issues (quoted by Wikipedia).

queue.title: SOCAPALM Palm Oil Plantations
queue.place: SOCAPALM plantations, Littoral and South regions, Cameroon
lenders: Bolloré and Socfin group holding companies (France, Belgium, Luxembourg) (foreign investors)
queue.confidence_note: The French NCP found breaches of the Guidelines, but the sources give no figures for land lost or pollution levels; details of the harm are the complainants'.

queue.title: Greece's Third Bailout (ESM) Pension and Tax Measures
queue.place: Athens, Greece
queue.confidence_note: The ESM was the only lender; VOA names the IMF alongside the EU as demanding the surplus target, but the IMF disbursed no money under this programme. The specific supplementary-pension cuts reported by To Vima were Greek legislation to meet the MoU's pension savings, not a figure set in the MoU. The labour minister disputed the size of cuts.

queue.title: WWF-Supported Ecoguards and the Baka, South-East Cameroon
queue.place: Lobéké, Boumba-Bek and Nki national parks, East Region, Cameroon
queue.confidence_note: The panel did not determine whether the alleged abuses occurred and saw no evidence WWF staff took part; its findings concern WWF's knowledge and continued support.

queue.title: SMB bauxite mining in Boké and its bank lenders
queue.place: Katougouma, Dapilon and villages along SMB's mining roads, Boké prefecture, Guinea
lenders: International Finance Corporation (IFC), through ICICI Bank
BNP Paribas, Credit Suisse, DZ Bank, Standard Chartered, Export-Import Bank of China and others
Crédit Agricole, China CITIC Bank, ING, Banco do Brasil and others
queue.confidence_note: The financing was general corporate lending to consortium members; no source shows the money was earmarked for SMB. The IFC link runs through a single loan to ICICI and rests on Inclusive Development International. SMB denies harming air quality and says water scarcity has several causes. IFC told Inclusive Development International in April 2017 that ICICI had repaid its IFC loans early; the date of repayment was not given.

queue.title: Kaltim Prima Coal and the Dayak Basap of Keraitan
queue.place: Keraitan and Tebangan Lembak villages, Bengalon, Kutai Timur, East Kalimantan, Indonesia
lenders: Bank of America, BNP Paribas, BPCE and other banks
queue.confidence_note: IFC did not dispute its exposure through Raiffeisen but said that investment was meant for the bank's European subsidiaries, and that Axis's bond money was limited to India; Inclusive Development International found no such limit in the bond circular. The financing went to KPC's owners, not to the mine as a project.

queue.title: Karuturi's Gambella farm and the ICICI loans
queue.place: Gambella region, Ethiopia
queue.confidence_note: Karuturi denied wrongdoing and said it worked only on land free of community claims and had pulled back from the Baro river. The IFC-ICICI-Karuturi chain rests on Inclusive Development International alone, and ICICI's loans were general corporate loans. IFC said in April 2017 that ICICI had repaid its IFC loans early.

queue.title: Vietnam Rubber Group concessions in Cambodia
queue.place: Kratie, Ratanakiri and Kampong Thom provinces, Cambodia
lenders: Vietinbank, with International Finance Corporation (IFC) equity
queue.confidence_note: Deutsche Bank says it only held shares for fund investors. The IFC link is indirect, through its stake in Vietinbank, and rests on Inclusive Development International; CAO found in a separate case that IFC's Vietinbank tie did not justify investigating Lower Sesan 2. The Tan Bien eviction (2009) came before IFC's 2011 Vietinbank stake; the other land losses were documented in 2012.

queue.title: Vinci's Moscow–St Petersburg Motorway Concession and the Khimki Forest
queue.place: Khimki Forest, Moscow Oblast, Russia
queue.confidence_note: Vinci's lead role and the forest clearance are documented. The attacks on journalists are thought to be linked to the protests, but no attacker is tied to the company, Beketov's beating came before Vinci's 2009 contract, and Vinci denies any connection; the route was chosen by the Russian authorities.

queue.title: Balhaf LNG Plant Used as a Detention Site
queue.place: Yemen LNG plant, Balhaf, Shabwah, Yemen
lenders: TotalEnergies (France) and French export credit guarantees
queue.confidence_note: The abuses were by UAE-led forces during the war after the plant was requisitioned, not by the company; Total says it lacks control over the site and was not aware of the abuses until November 2019. The export credit figure comes from Le Monde as cited by ECA Watch.

queue.title: Lawpita (Baluchaung) Hydropower, Karenni State
queue.place: Lawpita and Mobye dam area, Balu Chaung River, Karenni (Kayah) State, Myanmar
lenders: Government of Japan (war reparations, 1986 loan, 2002 grant)
queue.confidence_note: Timing and causation are uncertain: Japan paid for the 1960 construction and a 1986 renovation, and granted repair money in 2002, while the documented abuses (early-1990s relocations, landmines, 1998 water diversion) were carried out by the Myanmar army securing the plant, not by the funders. The harm accounts come from an armed opposition party and a Karenni research group; the 12,558 figure comes from EJAtlas's summary of the KDRG report, not seen directly.

queue.title: SOMAGEC Quarry Blasting and 2024 Arrests, Annobón
queue.place: Annobón island (San Antonio de Palé), Equatorial Guinea
lenders: SOMAGEC (Sociétés Maghrébiennes de Génie Civil), Morocco-based contractor (foreign company)
queue.confidence_note: The arrests and their arbitrary character are documented by a UN working group. The environmental harm rests on allegations received by UN rapporteurs and community reports; SOMAGEC denies it and says the quarry has been closed since 2019. SOMAGEC's Equatorial Guinea company says it is Equatoguinean, not Moroccan. SOMAGEC is a building contractor that also opened and ran the quarry and the island's water works; no outside lender is recorded.

queue.title: Hatgyi Dam Site Offensive and Karen Displacement, Salween River
queue.place: Hatgyi dam site, Myaing Gyi Ngu area, Hlaingbwe township, Karen State, Myanmar
lenders: Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT), Thai state utility (foreign investor)
Sinohydro Corporation (China), majority shareholder (Chinese state company)
queue.confidence_note: The displacement is documented, but the claim that the 2009 offensive was meant to clear the dam area comes from the KNU and environmental groups; the Myanmar army's war with the KNU predates the dam. The Thai government said in 2009 it was waiting for a committee's recommendations (IPS).

queue.title: Foreign-Owned Fishmeal Factories, Nouadhibou
queue.place: Fishmeal and fish oil plants, northern Nouadhibou, Dakhlet Nouadhibou, Mauritania
lenders: Poly Hong Dong Pelagic Fishery (China) and other foreign fishmeal investors (foreign investors)
companies: Poly Hong Dong Pelagic Fishery Co.
queue.confidence_note: The foreign investment and the factories' growth are documented; the health figures come only from EJAtlas, and not all of the 30-plus plants are foreign-owned. The Africa Defense Forum is published by US Africa Command.

queue.title: Pinpet Iron Mine and Steel Works Land Seizures, Taunggyi
queue.place: Mount Pinpet, near Taunggyi, southern Shan State, Myanmar
lenders: Tyazhpromexport (Russia), state-owned equipment supplier and investor (foreign company)
queue.confidence_note: Land and displacement figures come from one field-research group, the Pa-Oh Youth Organization, whose report DVB covered in 2009; they were not independently confirmed, and Wikipedia draws on the same report. The PYO says company investments and control were hard to confirm because of government secrecy; it describes Tyazhpromexport as investing equipment worth US$150 million.

queue.title: Phosphate Mining around Koudiadiène, Thiès
queue.place: SEPHOS and AIG phosphate mines, Koudiadiène, Thiafathie and Lam-Lam, Chérif Lô commune, Tivaouane department, Senegal
lenders: Tervalis group (Spain), parent of SEPHOS SA, and African Investment Group (90% Polish-owned) (foreign investors)
queue.confidence_note: Most findings come from one field study by AEFJN and CICODEV with villagers' testimony, which EJAtlas also draws on; they were not independently confirmed. SEPHOS disputes the hiring claims, saying 80% of its recruits come from Lam-Lam and Baliga and that youth of Koudiadiène lack the skills.

queue.title: Tigyit Coal Mine and Power Plant, Pinlaung
queue.place: Tigyit village, Pinlaung township, southern Shan State, Myanmar
lenders: China National Heavy Machinery Corporation (CHMC), Chinese state company (foreign builder and operator)
queue.confidence_note: Most figures come from one field-research group, the Pa-Oh Youth Organization ('Poison Clouds'); Wikipedia draws on the same report. The report notes unconfirmed claims that CHMC transferred its shares to Eden Group in 2010. No Chinese state loan is documented in these sources.

queue.title: Rare Earth Mining in Kachin Special Region 1
queue.place: Kachin Special Region 1, near Pangwa and Chipwi, Kachin State, Myanmar
lenders: Chinese investors behind Myanmar front companies (foreign investment)
queue.confidence_note: Radio Free Asia's 2022 reporting separately confirms forest loss, landslides and water contamination, and quotes a local activist and a mine worker saying the main owners are Chinese. The foreign-investment link rests mainly on Global Witness's investigation; the companies are registered as Burmese and the investment is not on paper. Global Witness reports that Chinese state-linked entities may have funded the start of operations but does not document a specific lender.

queue.title: Rafey Landfill Concession and the Santiago Waste Pickers
queue.place: Rafey landfill, Cienfuegos district, Santiago de los Caballeros, Dominican Republic
lenders: Green Wheels Dominicana (United States origin) and Lavo Investments (Italy) (foreign investors)
queue.confidence_note: The 2017 removal and arrest are described by the pickers' association, a party to the dispute, and the mayor's statements confirm police action and the handover to Cilpen Global but do not give numbers. The link between Cilpen Global and the foreign firms rests on the association's statement (and EJAtlas). The 2014 injuries and shooting rest on EJAtlas alone and are not used.

queue.title: Busanga dam: village homes destroyed for the Sicomines power plant
queue.place: Kamalenge, Monga Lubuza, Wafinya and nearby villages, Busanga, Lualaba province, DR Congo
lenders: Sinohydro and China Railway Group (Sicohydro joint venture)
queue.confidence_note: Counts of destroyed buildings (more than 1,000 in one statement, about 900 homes in another) come from civil society statements reported by Actualite.cd; no company or government count or response was found. Which Chinese bank, if any, lent for the dam is not stated in the sources; the link is through the Chinese state companies that co-own and build it.

queue.title: Rempang Eco-City, Xinyi's Glass Factory Plan and the 2023 Crackdown
queue.place: Rempang Island, Batam, Riau Islands, Indonesia
queue.confidence_note: The outside link is disputed: the Xinyi pledge was announced by Indonesian officials and reported by the press, but Xinyi says it signed no agreement or contract and did not initiate the eco-city. The eviction orders, tear gas and arrests are documented; how many families have actually moved is not given in the sources.

queue.title: Stora Enso's Eucalyptus Land Leases in Guangxi
queue.place: Hepu County, Beihai, Guangxi, China
queue.confidence_note: The legal findings come from an NGO study of Stora Enso's own land contracts; violence against villagers rests mainly on EJAtlas and is not tied in these sources to Stora Enso staff. Stora Enso's response is not given in detail.

queue.title: Southern Cardamom REDD+ Carbon Project and the Chong People
queue.place: Southern Cardamom, Koh Kong Province, Cambodia
lenders: Wildlife Works Carbon and Everland (United States), with Wildlife Alliance (US NGO) (foreign investor)
queue.confidence_note: Wildlife Alliance disputes the HRW findings. The outside parties are a US conservation NGO, a for-profit US carbon developer that is an investor (Wildlife Works Carbon) and a US credit broker, so the case is filed as foreign investment (fdi) rather than a foundation; the evictions were carried out with state rangers and military police.

queue.title: Areva's COMUF Uranium Mine at Mounana and Its Former Workers
queue.place: Mounana, Haut-Ogooué, Gabon
companies: COMUF (Compagnie des mines d'uranium de Franceville)
queue.confidence_note: The link between the illnesses and uranium exposure is disputed: Areva says no radiation-linked occupational disease has been found, and experts note smoking and other factors can cause such disease. The death toll comes from the former workers' association.

queue.title: Nordgold's Bissa Gold Mine: Two Villages Moved
queue.place: Bissa and Imiougou villages, Sabcé commune, Bam province, Burkina Faso
queue.confidence_note: Nordgold confirms it relocated the Bissa and Imiougou villages. The losses (fallow land left uncompensated, suspected well pollution) come from EJAtlas and the Swiss NGOs' field research, which Nordgold calls inaccurate anecdotal evidence; the 2016 road blockade (AIB) records a land grievance but no independent finding of loss was found.

queue.title: Kangqiao Lead Poisoning: Children Near a Johnson Controls Battery Plant
queue.place: Kangqiao, Pudong New Area, Shanghai, China
companies: Shanghai Xinmingyuan Automobile Parts Co Ltd
queue.confidence_note: The government blamed three plants, one US-owned and two Chinese, and did not apportion shares; it called the link to Johnson Controls' emissions "quite obvious" and the link to the local firm Xinmingyuan "definite". Johnson Controls denies its plant caused the exposure. The government's findings are reported through a single AFP story. EJAtlas says the official investigation identified Shanghai Johnson Controls as the major source of lead contamination, a finding not confirmed in a second source.

queue.title: Mukumbi settlement burned on the Mutoshi copper-cobalt concession
queue.place: Mukumbi (former settlement), Mutoshi concession, about 5 km north-east of Kolwezi, Lualaba, DR Congo
lenders: Chemaf (Chemical of Africa SA), owned by a Dubai-headquartered parent (foreign investor)
queue.confidence_note: Accounts of who destroyed Mukumbi conflict: former residents say Republican Guard soldiers burned it after company representatives, accompanied by police, told them to leave; Chemaf denies any wrongdoing, liability, involvement in the destruction or directing military forces, and says it was not aware of a village called Mukumbi until 2019. The destruction itself is supported by satellite images reviewed by Amnesty. The account rests on one field investigation (Amnesty International and IBGDH). Chemaf acquired the lease in June 2015, before the November 2016 burning.

queue.title: Metalkol tailings project: Tshamundenda farmers' fields bulldozed under military guard
queue.place: Tshamundenda, near the Metalkol RTR concession, about 5 km north-west of Kolwezi, Lualaba, DR Congo
lenders: Eurasian Resources Group (Luxembourg; largest shareholder the government of Kazakhstan), owner of Metalkol (foreign investor)
queue.confidence_note: ERG says the farmers had already been compensated by a previous operator and were occupying land illegally, and that it did not control the soldiers; the farmers dispute this. The account rests on one NGO field investigation.

queue.title: Haiyu heavy-sands mining and the 2015 flood at Nagonha
queue.place: Nagonha, Sangage, Angoche district, Nampula, Mozambique
lenders: Hainan Haiyu Mining (China), parent of Haiyu Mozambique Mining (foreign investor)
queue.confidence_note: Amnesty concludes the mining 'likely contributed significantly' to the flood; Haiyu denies it, calling the flood a natural event not seen in 100 years. All harm figures come from Amnesty's field research (the Mail & Guardian piece is by Amnesty staff). Amnesty's UK press release gives 270 people made homeless while its report and later statement give about 290. The concession was awarded on 19 December 2011, before the flood.

queue.title: Damietta Fertiliser Plant Protests
queue.place: Damietta and Ras El-Bar, Egypt
queue.confidence_note: The company denied harm, citing a Ministry of Environment report and offering a WHO inspection. Agrium held 26% of state-owned MOPCO in 2011 and was not the operator, though Ahram Online calls the plant Canadian-Egyptian. The death and arrests are reported by a witness and one campaign group; pollution damage is claimed by residents and was not measured. Ahram Online notes some observers tied the opposition to landowners and businessmen with interests in Ras El-Bar.

queue.title: Tangier Candle Protests against Amendis (Veolia)
queue.place: Tangier, Morocco
queue.confidence_note: Crowd sizes differ: The Moroccan Times cites local reports of at least 60,000; Reuters says thousands. Amendis blames a 2014 state pricing change and summer demand. The only per-household figure is one resident's account on an undated page, so it may not be from 2015.

queue.title: Kyaukphyu Port and Zone: Farmland Taken, Fishing Restricted
queue.place: Kyaukphyu, Rakhine State, Myanmar
queue.confidence_note: CITIC puts land acquisition and resettlement on the government, citing project agreements. The port was not yet built in 2019, so the fishing limits are not shown to come from CITIC's work; they rest on villagers' accounts. Reports differ on how much land was taken: 1,800 acres (2020) against about 250 acres of farmland in the project area (2021). No outside lender's loan was confirmed; the link is the foreign investor, in place from 2015.

queue.title: Teluk Sepang Coal Plant: Fishers' Losses and Dead Turtles
queue.place: Teluk Sepang, Bengkulu, Sumatra, Indonesia
lenders: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China
queue.confidence_note: The loans (October 2016) and construction (February 2017, AidData) precede the harm, so the link is firm. The harm is not: each item comes from fishers or campaign groups. The plant's engineer says its activities did not cause the turtle deaths, and a provincial test found the outlet within standards at 35°C. A Bengkulu University lecturer would not link the deaths to the plant without further examination; Kanopi suspects heat from the outlet. The conservation agency's lab report was unreleased in January 2020. PowerChina and Intraco Penta did not answer the China-Global South Project. That article states catch in tonnes (8.6 million to 2.4 million), a unit that looks too large, so no figures are used; it also dates construction to 2020.

queue.title: HSBC's Loans to Sarawak's Logging Companies
queue.place: Ulu Belaga and other logging areas, Sarawak, Malaysia
queue.confidence_note: Rests mainly on Global Witness's own investigation; its earnings figure is an estimate. HSBC would not confirm clients, said it is 'not accurate' that they break its policy and that 99% of its forestry customers comply or nearly comply. Chief Minister Taib called corruption claims untrue and Ta Ann denied bribery.

queue.title: Foreign Banks and the Myanmar Junta's Arms Purchases
queue.place: Myanmar
lenders: 16 banks in seven countries; Singapore-based banks
queue.confidence_note: The bank figures come from one UN expert's report, which says banks facilitated purchases and have a duty not to facilitate crimes. These are payments, not loans, and no page says a payment caused a given attack. Siam Commercial Bank declined to comment at once.

queue.title: Nexen Block 14, Hadramawt: oily water floods farms
queue.place: Blocks 14 (Masila) and 51, near Raseb, Hadramawt, Yemen
queue.confidence_note: The spill and farm losses rest on OCCRP's investigation, which draws on the unpublished report, the arbitration and residents. The Sana'a Center confirms Nexen's scale of produced water and a Paris case, but not this spill. Nexen admitted pumping wastewater below a freshwater aquifer in the 1990s and said it caused no damage. CNOOC did not respond. The health link is unproven.

queue.title: Desert Dumps: EU Money and Migrant Round-Ups in North Africa
queue.place: Sfax, Tunisia; Rabat, Morocco; Nouakchott, Mauritania
queue.confidence_note: European officials denied that EU funds were used to violate rights, and Commission spokeswoman Ana Pisonero said partner countries remain sovereign states with control of their forces. Two EU sources said it is 'impossible' to fully account for how the money was used. The vehicle link is a match of make and model, not a proven serial number. The reports carry no reply from Morocco, Tunisia or Mauritania.

queue.title: UN Drug Office Support for Iran's Anti-Narcotics Police
queue.place: Iran
lenders: UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
queue.confidence_note: Denmark publicly acknowledged that its donations were leading to executions (Human Rights Watch). UNODC spokesman David Dadge said the funds strengthen the capacity to interdict drugs and that the programme has a social part for prevention and treatment (VICE). No source ties a named execution to an arrest made with this equipment, and no official statement links the funding directly to executions.

queue.title: Nech Sar: Guji Homes Burned Before African Parks Took Over
queue.place: Nech Sar National Park, Ethiopia
queue.confidence_note: African Parks was not managing the park at the time of the burning, and Ethiopian authorities carried it out. African Parks' 2004 annual report called the resettlement an 'internal affair' of the governments, its founder said it disassociated itself from forced eviction attempts, and it said it would never be involved in political questions. The link is its agreement, signed nine months earlier, which tied the takeover to completed resettlement. The Refugees International report is known through these pages.

queue.title: Con Son Tiger Cages and US Aid to South Vietnam's Prisons
queue.place: Con Son Island, Vietnam
queue.confidence_note: The cages, the visit and USAID's prison money are on the record. The harm found in 1970 predates the 1971 contract, so that contract is not tied to it. GAO found no record of tiger cage purchases among the officials it asked, and says the $400,000 was paid in local currency. Luce, a participant and campaigner, says the money came from Food for Peace, the new cages were smaller, and the US 'paid the salaries of the torturers'; no US government document cited here confirms those three points. The French built the original cages (CounterPunch). US officials at the time defended the prison.

queue.title: East New Britain Palm Oil: Maybank Credit and Police Raid at Watwat
queue.place: Watwat village, East New Britain, Papua New Guinea
companies: ENB Resources Group (ENBPOL), with Tobar Investment and Tzen Niugini
queue.confidence_note: ENB said 'we generally deny all the allegations', and that both companies deny using police for violence or illegal detention, calling the findings baseless. Tobar and Lamur did not reply. The accounts come from one investigation, including undercover recordings. The credit agreement predates the raid by four years, and the bank does not confirm it.

queue.title: A Kigali Bank in the War Economy of Eastern Congo, in a UN Report
queue.place: Bukavu, DR Congo
lenders: Banque de commerce, du développement et d'industrie (BCDI), Kigali
queue.confidence_note: At the Council on 3 May 2001 Rwanda called the report imprecise and unconvincing, Uganda said most of the evidence was rumour or lies, and Burundi said the data were not enough to accuse it (S/PV.4317). The report also says Banque commerciale du Congo 'is linked to the Belgolaise' and that Bank Bruxelles Lambert 'handles some' of Aziza Kulsum Gulamali's transactions, with no finding of wrongdoing or knowledge, so those banks are not listed as funders. This account rests on a mirror copy that ends at paragraph 156; the rest of the report, including its conclusions, was not checked against the UN file.

national_index_routes_tested_17_nov_2026.the finding: The endpoint round 38 found on Kenya Law is not Kenya's. kenyalaw.org runs the peachjam platform, and ten other national judgment indexes answer the identical path /search/api/documents/?search=. All ten were tested on 17 Nov 2026 and all ten returned JSON with judgments in results_html. One route therefore opens Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Ghana, Malawi, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Lesotho, Zimbabwe and Namibia as well as Kenya.
national_index_routes_tested_17_nov_2026.the correction to round 38's note: It called Kenya Law phrase-exact. It is not, unless the phrase is quoted. Unquoted, 'Kenya Informal Settlements Improvement Project' returns the 10,000 cap; quoted, it returns 21, and those 21 are the judgments that name the project. Always send the phrase in double quotes, URL-encoded as %22.
national_index_routes_tested_17_nov_2026.the trap: The ordinary /search/?q= page on every one of these sites is JavaScript-rendered and carries no results in its HTML — zero result links, a Vue app shell. A writer reading that page would record an absence. That is the thirteenth time on this map.
national_index_routes_tested_17_nov_2026.a live hit on the first card tried: kisip-informal-settlements-fatalities, top of this queue at 100% lender sources, has judgments on Kenya Law naming the Kenya Informal Settlements Improvement Project (Obul & 4 others, 2018 KEHC 4492 and a 2019 ruling). Not yet read or written to the card — that is round 39's work.
